title: Steady reservoir-mediated self-trapping of polariton condensates
authors: Pavel N. Kozhevin, Oleg I. Utesov, Igor S. Aranson, Sergey V. Koniakhin, Anton V. Nalitov
abstract: Nonequilibrium bosonic condensates of exciton-polaritons generated by tightly focused incoherent optical beams are typically expected to form a stationary ballistically expanding state with the notable exception of experimentally observed compact self-trapped states [Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 047401 (2019)]. We show that the back-action of the condensate on the optically pumped excitonic reservoir via bosonic stimulated scattering can cause local reservoir depletion, producing a steady condensate confined in a self-induced potential trap. Notably, this self-trapped state is formed by persistent converging rather than radially expanding polariton currents and exists even below the conventionally defined condensation threshold. This state remains steady over nanosecond-scale times and is eventually ejected from the self-induced trap due to a bullet-type instability, enabling spiking neuromorphic dynamics in networks of polariton condensates.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes polariton condensates, showing that the interaction with the optical reservoir can induce a self-trapping mechanism. This mechanism allows the condensate to form a stable, compact state with converging currents, even when the pump power is below the standard condensation threshold. The findings are crucial for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics and potential applications in neuromorphic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation and stability of self-trapped states in polariton condensates, contrasting them with the conventionally expected ballistically expanding state.
main_result: Self-trapped states, driven by local reservoir depletion, can form stable, compact condensates even below the linear condensation threshold, exhibiting converging polariton currents.
method: The analysis employs the extended Gross-Pitaevskii Equation (eGPE) model, utilizing stability analysis (Bogoliubov-de Gennes) and examining stationary solutions in the deeply nonlinear regime.
model_or_system: The system models nonequilibrium exciton-polariton condensates, treated as a two-component system coupled to an incoherent optical reservoir, governed by coupled evolution equations.
key_observables: Condensate density, polariton currents (converging vs. expanding), condensate energy, and the existence/stability of self-trapped vs. ballistic solutions.
important_parameters: Condensation threshold ($p_{th}$), pump spot size ($R$), self-interaction strength ($\xi$), and reservoir coupling parameters ($\epsilon, a$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as the Gaussian ansatz for stationary modes and the adiabatic elimination of the reservoir in certain limits.
figures_summary: Figures compare self-trapped (hole-burning) vs. ballistic states, show stability diagrams mapping stable/unstable regions, and illustrate the evolution of polariton currents and density profiles.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the eGPE model, deriving simplified dynamical equations, performing stability analyses (BdG), and finally mapping out the phase diagram showing the coexistence and stability of the self-trapped state below the linear threshold.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics in cavity quantum electrodynamics systems, providing a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how reservoir coupling can stabilize exotic, non-trivial spatial structures in bosonic condensates.
